title: Procurement and Decellularization of Rat Hindlimbs Using an Ex Vivo Perfusion-Based Bioreactor for Vascularized Composite Allotransplantation
protocol: Prepare 50 mL of 5% heparinized saline.
Take out 2.5 mL of saline solution using a 5 mL syringe and discard.
Add 2.5 mL of heparin to the saline bag.
Invert the saline bag to mix its contents.
Place a cadaveric rat in a supine position under a blue pad.
Shave the hindlimb and groin area circumferentially using an electric shaver and remove hair.
Bring the rat to the surgical station.
Apply Povidone iodine scrub solution using a gauze to the hindlimb and groin area.
Subsequently, apply 70% isopropyl alcohol to wipe off the scrub solution using gauze.
Discard the blue pad from step 1.2 and change into new, sterile gloves.
Make a skin incision using a #10 surgical blade and a #3 blade runner along the inguinal ligament level, moving from a lateral to a medial direction.
Use Adson forceps to hold the surrounding skin to ensure a smooth incision.
Use blunt dissection to carefully dissect through the fat when the underlying fat is exposed.
Locate the superior epigastric vessels.
Dissect proximally using microscissors to expose the femoral nerve, artery, and vein at the inguinal ligament level.
Identify the femoral vessels under a dissection microscope.
Dissect the artery and vein proximally using fine forceps to obtain sufficient length from the bifurcation points of the arterial network.
Ligate the femoral artery separately using 6-0 sutures.
Ligate the femoral vein separately using 6-0 sutures.
Conduct circumferential dissection around the remainder of the hindlimb without disrupting the ligated femoral vessels.
Transect the femoral bone mid-length using a bone cutter.
Transect the ligated femoral vessels below the ligatures using microscissors.
Cannulate the femoral artery using a 24 G angiocatheter under the dissection microscope.
Insert the cannula carefully using fine forceps.
Flush with heparinized saline until clear outflow is observed from the femoral vein.
Secure the cannula by tying one suture around the cannulated vessel.
Tie another suture distally around the cannula itself.
Ensure the cannula is placed proximally to prevent blocking the bifurcation points.
Submerge the procured hindlimbs in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) until decellularization.
In a 6 L glass flask, dissolve 12.5 g of SDS powder in 5 L of ultrapure distilled water to prepare a 0.25% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) reservoir.
Cover the opening of the 6 L flask with parafilm to seal it.
In a 1 L glass jar, dissolve 2.5 g of SDS in 1 L of ultrapure distilled water to prepare a separate 0.25% SDS solution.
Add a stir bar to mix the 1 L SDS solution on a magnetic stirrer until all the SDS is dissolved.
Prepare 1 L of 0.25% SDS solution by mixing 990 mL of 1x PBS solution and 10 mL of Antibiotic-Antimycotic (AA) solution in a 1 L flask.
Prepare another 500 ml of 1x PBS + 1% AA solution using 495 mL of 1x PBS solution and 5 mL of AA.
Prepare 200 mL of 1% peracetic acid (PAA)/4% ethanol (EtOH) solution under a fume hood.
Drill three holes (1/4 inch) at the labeled locations on a 500 mL chamber.
Remove and discard excess plastic from the drilled holes.
Spray and wipe the chamber with 70% ethanol.
Cut three 5 cm long silicone tubes.
Insert one silicone tube halfway into each port of the chamber.
Connect a male Luer connector to Port A facing inside the chamber and a female Luer connector on the other end outside the chamber.
Connect a female Luer connector at Port B and Port C on the ends of the tubes facing out of the chamber.
Drill one hole on the surface of an air-tight lid for the plastic container.
Cut a 3 cm silicone tube.
Insert the silicone tube into the hole of the lid, ensuring approximately 2 cm is located out of the lid.
Sterilize both the chamber and the lid with tubing.
Cut two 30 cm silicone tubes using scissors.
Connect a 1/16 inch to a 1/8 inch connector on one end of each tube.
Cut two 12 cm silicone tubes using scissors.
Connect a 1/16 inch to a 1/8 inch connector on one end of both tubes.
Connect a male Luer connector on the other end of one tube and a female Luer connector to the other tube.
Sterilize all tubing material from previous steps.
Include two 3-stop pump tubings (1.85 mm) in the sterilization process.
Prepare three 3-way stopcocks for the decellularization setup.
Remove the filter from two 1 mL serological pipettes.
Attach one syringe filter and two 1 mL serological pipettes to the setup.
Screw sterilized chamber onto three single-use 3-way stopcocks at inlet, outlet, and replenishing lines.
Cap remaining ports of the stopcock for the replenishing line to prevent leakage.
Connect tubes from step 4.8 to the stopcocks at inlet and outlet lines.
Attach peristaltic tubing to the connected tubes.
Place cassette on the peristaltic pump without securing it with tubing yet.
Connect one tube from step 4.7 to the end of the peristaltic tubing of the outlet line.
Connect a 1 mL serological pipette on the other end.
Suspend the end attached with a serological pipette in the waste reservoir flask.
Repeat step 4.7 for the inlet line.
Suspend the end of the tube attached to the serological pipette into the detergent reservoir.
Seal the opening of the detergent reservoir flask with parafilm immediately.
Add 0.25% SDS from the 1 L glass jar (step 3.2) into the bioreactor chamber at the halfway level.
Take the procured hindlimb using Adson forceps and suspend it into the bioreactor chamber carefully.
Use two pairs of Adson forceps to guide the cannulated portion of the hindlimb to the inlet line.
While holding the cannula with one pair of forceps, use the other pair of forceps to twist and secure the inlet line to the cannula.
Ensure the cannula is not pulled or twisted to prevent decannulation.
Add more 0.25% SDS from the 1 L glass jar to fully submerge the limb as needed.
Ensure the outlet port is also submerged in the bioreactor reservoir to ensure consistent outflow is maintained.
Attach a single-use syringe filter to the ventilation port on the lid of the bioreactor chamber, referring to step 4.4 and step 4.5.
Secure the lid on the bioreactor and ensure the chamber is sealed from all sides.
Use a new, single-use 10 mL syringe to draw detergent from the reservoir using the 3-way stopcock at the inlet line.
Insert the drawn fluid into the 3-way stopcock at the outlet line.
Ensure that there is detergent present throughout the tubing at both the inlet and outlet lines.
Press down and secure the cassettes with the tubing into the peristaltic pump.
Turn the peristaltic pump on using the power button.
Proceed to the second tab on the peristaltic pump screen using the arrow key.
Set the perfusion rate for the first channel at 1 mL/min in flow rate mode.
Repeat setting the perfusion rate of 1 mL/min for the second channel.
Calibrate the peristaltic pump to ensure consistent fluid delivery between channels.
Ensure that the tubing ID is set to 1.85 mm.
Begin decellularization via machine perfusion at 1 mL/min for both inlet and outlet lines by pressing the power button on the keypad.
Monitor and ensure that the flow rate is consistent at both inlet and outlet lines.
Continue decellularization and monitor daily.
Replenish the bioreactor reservoir with 1 L of 0.25% SDS as needed through the replenishing port.
Monitor for a white, translucent appearance indicating successful decellularization by day 5.
Replace the detergent reservoir with the 1x PBS + 1% AA reservoir.
Seal the opening of the flask with parafilm.
Begin perfusion using 1x PBS + 1% AA at a rate of 1 mL/min for 2 days.
Replace the 1x PBS + 1% AA reservoir with a 0.1% PAA/4% EtOH reservoir.
Begin perfusion using 0.1% PAA/4% EtOH at a rate of 1 mL/min for 2 hours.
Disconnect the hindlimb from the inlet line using two pairs of sterile Adson forceps, twisting the inlet line with one pair and holding the cannula with the other.
Store the limb in a 500 mL glass jar containing 1x PBS + 1% AA at 4 °C until further use.
